chunks: Khasa'il of al-Saduq: Ibn al-Walid from al-Saffar from al-Barqi from Ismail ibn Mihran from Ubays ibn Hisham from more than one from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The reciters of the Qur'an are three: A man who recited the Qur'an and took it as merchandise, attracted the rulers by it, and gained prominence over the people by it; and a man who recited the Qur'an and preserved its letters but neglected its bounds; and a man who recited the Qur'an and applied the medicine of the Qur'an to the ailment of his heart, so he kept awake by it his night, thirsted by it his day, stood in prayer by it in his mosques, and abandoned his bed for it. Because of them does Allah the All-Mighty, the Almighty, avert tribulation, and because of them does Allah grant victory over the enemies, and because of them does Allah send down rain from the sky. And by Allah, these reciters of the Qur'an are rarer than red sulphur.
ai.seo_question: What are the three categories of Qur'an reciters according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kulaynī’s *Al-Kāfī* (via al-Ṣadūq’s chain), Imam al-Bāqir (AS) delineates three tiers of Qur’anic reciters, contrasting the worldly merchant and the superficial memorizer with the true devotee who internalizes the text to cure the heart’s ailments. This third category, characterized by vigilance (*sahar*) and prayer (*qiyām*), is elevated above even red sulphur (*kibrīt al-ahmar*), serving as the divine instrument for averting calamities and bringing rain. The hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on *tadabbur* (reflection) and practical application of the Qur’an over mere recitation or memorization.
